events.title: Critical FortiMail Zero-Day Flaw Exploited in Attacks Allows Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Writes
events.summary: A critical zero‑day flaw in Fortinet FortiMail (CVE‑2026‑104286) allows unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary files, and it is actively exploited.
events.why_it_matters: The flaw has a CVSS score of 9.8 and is listed in CISA’s KEV catalog, indicating it is actively exploited. It allows unauthenticated attackers to write arbitrary files on the underlying system, which could lead to full compromise.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2026-104286 as exploited in the wild, added 2026-10-01, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2026-10-04.
CVE-2026-104286 is rated 9.8 (critical) under CVSS 3.1 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2026-104286 being exploited in the next 30 days at 2.2%.

events.title: Armatura LLC Armatura One
events.summary: Armatura LLC’s Armatura One access‑control system is vulnerable to multiple high‑severity exploits that could give attackers full control of the database and host. Versions below 4.7.2 (US) and 4.6.1 (USA) are affected by CVE‑2023‑46604 and related CVEs.
events.why_it_matters: The vulnerabilities have a CVSS score of 9.8 overall and CVE‑2023‑46604 scores 10.0, indicating critical risk. Exploitation could allow attackers to gain privileged access, execute arbitrary code, or take control of the physical access‑control system. Defenders should prioritize patching affected Armatura One installations.

claims.text: CISA lists CVE-2023-46604 as exploited in the wild, added 2023-11-02, with US federal agencies due to fix it by 2023-11-23.
CVE-2023-46604 is rated 10.0 (critical) under CVSS 3.1 by the CNA that assigned it.
FIRST's EPSS puts the chance of CVE-2023-46604 being exploited in the next 30 days at 100%, the highest of the 5 CVEs here.
A fix for org.apache.activemq:activemq-client (Maven) is published in 5.15.16, 5.16.7, 5.17.6 and 5.18.3, per GHSA-crg9-44h2-xw35.
